hero.title: Corporate readiness: from CV to your first 90 days
hero.subtitle: Write your CV, cover letter and interview answers in a document editor, and compare job offers in a working spreadsheet. Every task is checked and explained.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the interview pack and the final assessment.

faq.q: Will this get me a job?
faq.a: No course can promise that. It teaches the skills that make your applications and interviews stronger.
No. The course shows how to use projects, clubs and study as evidence.

faq.q: Does it cover a particular country's job market?
faq.a: It teaches general principles. Customs for CVs and salary vary by country, so research your local market.

activities.title: Write a one-page CV
activities.objective: Build a CV with a summary, achievements with numbers, skills and education.
activities.scenario: Write the CV of a fresh graduate, Arjun Rao, applying for a junior marketing role.
steps: Add a Heading 1 with a name.
Add Heading 2 sections: Summary, Experience, Skills, Education.
Under Experience, write at least three achievement bullets that start with an action verb and include a number.
Under Skills, list at least four skills.
Keep it between 120 and 330 words.

activities.title: Write a short cover letter
activities.objective: Write a letter that links your experience to the employer's need.
activities.scenario: Apply for a junior marketing role at a company called Greenleaf Foods.
steps: Start with Dear and a name or Hiring Manager.
In the first sentence name the role and where you saw it.
Write one paragraph linking your best achievement to the job.
Write a sentence on why this company.
End with a call to action such as I would welcome an interview, and Yours sincerely.

checks.hint: Include a measurable result.

checks.label: Why this company
checks.hint: Include the word because or admire.

activities.title: Compare two job offers
activities.objective: Compare total yearly value of two offers, including costs and benefits.
activities.scenario: You have two offers. One pays more but costs more to commute to. Work out which gives more money in your pocket and how it compares on a scorecard.
steps: In B7 total the yearly benefits in column B (salary, bonus, other).
In C7 do the same for offer C.
In B9 compute yearly commute cost: daily cost times working days.
In B10 compute net yearly value: total minus commute cost, and do the same in C10.
In B12 show the better offer with IF.

checks.label: B7 totals offer A
checks.hint: =SUM(B2:B5)

checks.label: C7 totals offer B
checks.hint: =SUM(C2:C5)

checks.label: B10 is the yearly commute for A
C10 is the yearly commute for B
B11 is net value of A
C11 is net value of B
B13 names the better offer
checks.hint: =IF(B11>C11,"Offer A","Offer B")
checks.explain: Choose the larger net value, then think about growth too.

activities.title: Write a 30-60-90 day plan
activities.objective: Plan what you will learn, deliver and improve in your first three months.
activities.scenario: You have just been offered a junior marketing role. Write your plan for the first 90 days.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'My 90-day plan'.
Add three Heading 2 sections: First 30 days, Days 31 to 60, Days 61 to 90.
Under each, write at least two actions in a bulleted list.
Include a goal that can be measured in the last section.
Keep it between 100 and 260 words.

checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for each phase.

checks.label: Phases in order
checks.hint: 30 days, then 60, then 90.

checks.hint: Use the bullet button.

checks.label: A measurable goal
checks.hint: Include a number in the final phase.

checks.label: Between 100 and 260 words

checks.explain: A plan should fit one page.

activities.title: Final project: your interview pack
activities.objective: Prepare a one-page pack for a real or imagined interview: pitch, three stories and questions to ask.
activities.scenario: You have an interview next week for a role you want. Write a one-page prep pack.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Interview pack'.
Add Heading 2 sections: My pitch, My stories, Questions to ask.
Under My pitch write 3 or 4 sentences about who you are, what you offer and why this role.
Under My stories list three one-line stories with results, each with a number.
Under Questions to ask list three questions.
Keep it between 130 and 320 words.
